LESSON: DIVISIONS OF THE BIBLE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible 3.1 Functions of the Bible (6 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, 
Topic 3.2: Divisions of the Bible

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Divisions of the Bible. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to know the books of the Bible?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the two divisions of the Bible
2. appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DIVISIONS OF THE BIBLE
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Divisions of the Bible helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

PART 1: Identify the two divisions of the Bible

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the two divisions of the Bible. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the two divisions of the Bible.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Divisions of the Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the two divisions of the Bible. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Divisions of the Bible in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Divisions of the Bible is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Divisions of the Bible” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the two divisions of the Bible)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Divisions of the Bible in your own words. (skill: appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Divisions of the Bible to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the two divisions of the Bible.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Divisions of the Bible from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Divisions of the Bible: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Divisions of the Bible?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to know the books of the Bible?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Divisions of the Bible means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the two divisions of the Bible.
5. Be able to: appreciate the Bible for reflective learning and living.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
